title: The Forming of the Natural Mind and the Two Trees
description: The opening teachings establish the foundational dualism. T1 (a creation-fall fragment) traces how the proprium asserts itself, draws claimed states upward, and is permitted to take shape so that within the formed vessel the discrimination can begin — the soul's first opening of sight within the molded form. T2 unfolds the Two Trees as five-membered organisms: one whole arrangement of perception that the Lord plants, with its five degrees ascending from reflection through counsel and teaching and thought up to mind; and the same five degrees turned the other way under self-love, with the rational organized as law of death, exchange and furnace, smoke-filled gehenna, stronghold, and clod. The two trees do not grow from one trunk; they stand distinct in origin, and the soul must learn to taste which is which.
